modified_caption: The pie chart illustrates the distribution of emotion categories in the IEMOCAP dataset, with percentages displayed relative to the number of utterances. Frustration is the largest category, accounting for approximately 25.1% of the data, followed by Neutral at 23.1%. Anger and Sadness are nearly equal, with Anger slightly higher at 15.9% and Sadness at 14.7%. Excitement and Happiness are the smallest categories, with Happiness at 10.1% and Excitement at 14.1%. Notably, the data suggests a consistent decline in positive emotions (Excitement and Happiness) compared to negative ones (Frustration, Anger, and Sadness). The chart provides a clear visual representation of the emotional distribution, with labels positioned outside each slice for clarity.

modifications.reality: Anger is actually 14.9%, not 15.9%. The modified caption inflates the value by 1%, creating a false anchor.
Happiness is actually 8.1%, not 10.1%. The modified caption inflates the value by 2%, creating a false anchor.

modifications.claim: The data suggests a consistent decline in positive emotions compared to negative ones.
modifications.reality: The chart does not show any trend or rate of change; it only displays static percentages. The claim about a 'consistent decline' is fabricated.
